title: Jayaswal Neco: AVOID — Promoter pledge 99.9% despite deleveraging.

body: On 8 Nov 2016 Rs 500/1,000 notes (~86% of currency by value) were withdrawn. Nifty: above 8,500 before the move (8 Nov close cited ~8,516-8,544) to a seven-month low of 7,908 on 26 Dec 2016, about -7%. Hardest hit: BSE Realty -17% (8 Nov - 26 Dec); microfinance and gold-loan NBFCs such as Bharat Financial Inclusion and Manappuram fell 40%+; consumer discretionary and cash-heavy sectors. By mid-Feb 2017 benchmarks were ~3% above their 8 Nov close; Bharat Financial and Manappuram had rallied ~60% from December lows - helped by a stemming of FPI outflows, a better-than-feared December-quarter, and strong domestic MF buying. 2017 then became a broad small-cap and realty rally: Nifty Realty +~97% (biggest in a decade), with small caps also surging (BSE Smallcap ~+60% in 2017, from memory). Analysts noted demonetisation plus GST deferred earnings recovery by ~3 quarters. Signal: the shock was a liquidity/sentiment hit, not a balance-sheet crisis, and domestic flows (SIPs, post-demonetisation 'financialisation of savings') were rising. Lesson: policy shocks that don't damage the banking system are usually bought within months; but the flood of domestic money that followed fed the 2017 small-cap froth that crashed in 2018.

data.lesson: non-systemic policy shocks are bought fast

title: Demonetisation shock (Nov 2016) and the 2017 smallcap/realty surge
